FIELD GUIDE / 04 · Embedded projects · separate from C++

CUnderstand the machine underneath.

C makes the relationship between a program and memory much more visible. It is a foundation for understanding firmware, low-level interfaces, and the constraints of small computers.

THE INVESTMENT

Why this deserves your time.

C becomes valuable when your aerospace curiosity reaches sensors, flight computers, embedded Linux, or resource-constrained devices. NASA’s core Flight System is a real example of a reusable flight-software framework built around C. UCSD’s MAE 144 description also connects robotics, embedded Linux, and C; requirements and offerings should be rechecked when you enroll.

Even if you eventually write more C++ or Python, C can improve your understanding of data representation, buffers, interfaces, and what an abstraction hides. It deserves focused study when you have an embedded goal, rather than a second introductory course competing with Python from day one.

Connect it to your existing tools

C relates to embedded firmware and operating-system interfaces. KiCad designs the electronics; C can program a controller on those electronics. The compiler, board support package, and hardware documentation are part of that workflow.

FROM SYNTAX TO SYSTEMS

Problems this helps you solve.

01

Sensor interfaces

Represent readings using explicit units and fixed-width integer types. Learn to distinguish a valid reading from an error or unavailable value.

02

Flight-software foundations

Explore NASA cFS documentation to see how reusable software components and platform abstractions support mission software. This is a later reading path, not a first project.

03

Telemetry formats

Decode a small simulated packet with documented fields, lengths, and byte order. Check the input before reading it.

04

Embedded experiments

Build a desktop-tested state machine, then adapt a small part to a microcontroller once you understand its hardware and development environment.

Evidence behind the ecosystem connections
NASA core Flight System ↗Arduino sketch build process ↗UCSD MAE course descriptions ↗

Projects described here are learning examples. A small demonstration does not establish flight readiness or production reliability.

THE HONEST LEARNING CURVE

What is hard—and why.

C has fewer language features than C++, but it exposes sharp edges. Arrays do not carry bounds automatically; pointers can outlive their data; integer conversions can surprise you; undefined behavior can invalidate reasoning about a program.

C and C++ are separate languages

They share history and syntax, but idioms and rules differ. Write clear C for a C project; learn modern C++ techniques in a C++ project.

Pointer knowledge needs careful practice

Draw the objects and their lifetimes. Use compiler warnings, a debugger, and sanitizers on supported desktop builds. Do not infer safety because one run happened to work.

Arduino is usually C++

Arduino sketches use C++ with a supporting framework. They can teach embedded concepts, but should not be labeled a pure C course.

A trap to avoid

Do not interpret a short C program as an easy or safe program. A ten-line parser can need more careful reasoning than a hundred-line high-level script.

LEARN IN LAYERS

A sequence with a visible result.

  1. 01 · Know the representation

    Types, functions, arrays, loops, integer ranges, warnings.

    YOUR PROOFWrite a checked conversion from integer sensor counts to a physical reading.

  2. 02 · Learn memory deliberately

    Pointers, length-aware APIs, stack lifetime, strings and buffers.

    YOUR PROOFWrite a function receiving both a data buffer and its length; reject short input.

  3. 03 · Make failure explicit

    Return codes, file input, tests, debugger and sanitizers where supported.

    YOUR PROOFTest empty data, a maximum value, and a malformed sample.

  4. 04 · Meet the hardware

    A small board, its datasheet, timing and I/O interfaces.

    YOUR PROOFLog one sensor reliably and document what happens if it is disconnected.

Advance by understanding, not a promised number of weeks. Rebuild a small example unaided, explain an error, and check a result before adding the next layer.

A SMALL WORKING IDEA

See the reason behind the code.

TRY THE IDEA

One byte can say several things.

Change the control and predict the result before looking.

In this invented format, bit 0 means sensor fault, bit 1 means stale data, and bit 2 means low battery. Real devices use their own documented layouts. Remaining bits are ignored here.

C / EXAMPLE TO STUDY
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

bool sensor_fault(uint8_t status) {
    const uint8_t fault_mask = 1u;
    return (status & fault_mask) != 0u;
}

Illustration runs in JavaScript in your browser. The C example is separate code to study and run in the appropriate environment.

CURATED, NOT COLLECTED

One main path. A few useful companions.

Use the C portion of CS50x or Beej’s Guide as your entry. Effective C is a strong paid companion once you want more systematic correctness and portability.

Costs checked November 4, 2026. Mixed free/paid resources can appear in both filters. Paid choices are optional; check school access and current terms before buying.

Course · beginnerRECOMMENDED START

CS50x — Introduction to Computer Science ↗

Harvard / David J. Malan

Builds a mental model of algorithms, memory and data structures through demanding exercises, including C.

How to use this resource

Focus initially on the C, arrays, algorithms and memory sections. It is a broader computer-science course, not a complete embedded-C curriculum.

Free course; optional paid edX certificate

Book · beginner

C Programming: A Modern Approach, 2nd edition ↗

K. N. King / W. W. Norton

Careful explanations and exercises make pointers, arrays and functions approachable.

How to use this resource

Use as your main C book if you prefer step-by-step depth. Its C99 coverage is foundational but not a guide to all later C standards.

Paid book

Online book · next

Beej’s Guide to C Programming ↗

Brian “Beej” Hall

An accessible explanation of C’s practical mechanics and deeper language topics.

How to use this resource

Use to reinforce pointers, structs and memory after the first lessons. Write and test your own tiny examples as you read.

Free online/PDF editions

Book · next

Effective C, 2nd edition ↗

Robert C. Seacord / No Starch Press

Adds modern C23 coverage and attention to correctness and professional programming practices.

How to use this resource

Read after basic C. Check which standard your compiler and embedded project support before using newer language features.

Paid book; sample material free

Reference · reference

C reference ↗

cppreference community

A precise lookup for C types, standard-library functions and version differences.

How to use this resource

Check array, string and integer behavior before trusting a low-level routine. Keep C rules separate from superficially similar C++ rules.

Free

Toolchain reference · reference

GCC online documentation ↗

GNU Compiler Collection

Documents language modes, diagnostics and compiler options used to build and inspect C programs.

How to use this resource

Use the manual matching your installed compiler. Learn warning options and debugging settings while building small host-side programs.

Free

THE NEXT SMALL WIN

Write a function that accepts an unsigned status byte and reports whether bit 0 is set. Test the values 0, 1, 2, and 3, and explain each result in binary.

A useful session ends with evidence

  1. Predict. What should happen, and why?
  2. Write. Spend most of the time in code.
  3. Check. Try a simple value and an awkward one.
  4. Explain. Describe the result in your own words.

Use AI for hints, explanations, and review. Attempt the task first, follow course rules, and finish by solving a small variant unaided.

EVIDENCE OF PROGRESS

Could you do it without a walkthrough?

A PROJECT WORTH KEEPING

Build a simulated environmental-sensor decoder. Specify a short packet format, validate its length, decode its status flags, and return a clear error for invalid input. Keep it on the desktop until the tests make sense.

Save the code, sample input, a short README, assumptions and units, a test case, and a result you can explain. That is stronger evidence than a completed playlist.
